Hi Maya / Helix SRE team,

Thanks again for choosing Redwood Dedicated. I'm handing off the implementation track from Sales/AE into our CS + Implementation squad so we can get the GPU pool provisioned and live quickly. Proposed high-level plan: a 3-week activation sprint followed by a 30-day stabilization window. Goals for sprint 0-2: 

- Provision dedicated GPU pool (4x A100-equivalent GPUs initially) in your primary region.
- Configure autoscaling + burst policy to allow short spikes without impacting latency SLAs.
- Network/IP allowlist, SSO + service-account setup, and SOC2 evidence handoff for procurement.
- Smoke tests: latency under 120ms p95 for 1k token generation, and sustained throughput validation.

Attached: Helix_HLX-MAP-v1.xlsx (mutual action plan), gpu-activation-checklist.md (initial checklist).

Questions for you to confirm so we start provisioning:
1) Preferred primary region (we suggested us-west-2 in pre-sales notes) — confirm or propose alternative.
2) Target minimum GPUs for baseline (recommended: 2) and peak burst tolerance (percentage of pool you want reserved vs burst to hosted fallback).
3) Procurement ETA for SOW/signature (we'll attach a draft SOW for review).

Proposed kickoff meeting slots next week: Mon 11/30 10:00-10:45 PT, Tue 12/1 08:00-08:45 PT. I'll send a calendar invite once we lock a slot.

Thanks — I'll loop in engineering to include a short pre-checklist for your infra team.

—Connor

Connor — quick internal tech notes to include in the join-kickoff pack. Posting so you can forward as needed.

Pre-provision checklist (engineering):
- Confirm VPC peering / private-link options and requested IP ranges from Helix.
- KMS/HSM keysetup for model keys and audit logging enabled (required for Private customers; still optional here but recommended).
- Pool sizing: start with 3x80GB GPUs, set min=2, desired=3, max=6 in autoscaler config.
- Autoscaler policy:
  - scale-up: trigger when queue length > 12 requests or avg GPU util > 70% for 2 minutes
  - scale-down: scale when util < 35% for 5 minutes; use cooldown 3 minutes
  - burst policy: allow up to +30% capacity by temporarily routing to reserved shared-hosted fallback; billable at hosted rate and bounded to 10 minutes per spike by default
- KV/prefix caching: enable prefix cache for deterministic prompts to reduce token spend during spikes
- Quantization: recommend INT8 inference profile for non-critical models to save 20-30% cost; confirm model quality evals with Helix before enabling globally

I'll attach the lightweight activation checklist (gpu-activation-checklist.md) to the kickoff invite. Owner suggestions: Laura (infra prechecks), Avery (runtime config + kernel selection), Connor (project coordination + procurement).

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime — Redwood Inference

Maya — thanks for the answers and for confirming the 11/30 kickoff slot. A couple of quick notes and attachments included: SOC2-summary-2026.pdf (SOC 2 high-level artifacts) and sow-draft-v1.docx (draft SOW for procurement).

Quick clarifications on burst behavior (summary):
- Burst to hosted fallback: short spikes are routed to our hosted pool only when the dedicated pool has exhausted configured burst headroom.
- Failback: requests automatically route back once dedicated pool has capacity; KV cache warming continues to reduce latency over the first 1-3 minutes post-failback.
- Billing: burst traffic is billed at our hosted per-token rate; we can include a monthly cap if needed.

Action item: Laura will publish the autoscaler thresholds and a one-pager on expected billing profile for burst in the kickoff attachments.

Please review the SOW and let us know redlines; procurement timeline noted. I'll attach the MAP and SOW to the meeting invite.

—Connor
